newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts close 4/32 lower, still look overcooked.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts close 4/32 lower, still look overcooked.

text.p: 1525 GMT - UK gilts slipped off their highs along with other European markets and settled 4/32 lower, hit by fall in U.S. Treasuries after higher-than-forecast labour costs data. Traders said even after spate of profittaking gilts are overcooked and further falls may follow.*June gilts settle at 113-09, down 4/32
Another broker said despite the spate of profittaking, gilts still looked top-heavy.
"Short-term gilts look overcooked," said Jonathan York, futures broker at Mees Pierson. "The market rallied up so fast yesterday it needs to go back and do a bit of work around the 112-16 level."
Most of Europe is closed on Thursday for the Ascension Day holiday and with little significant news scheduled gilts could drift lower.
"It's hard to see what is going to move things, but if the CBI (distributive trades) survey is very strong it could be the excuse for more profittaking," said the broker.
The survey is due at 1030 GMT.
The yield spread between gilts and Bunds edged out to 146 basis points compared with 145 on Tuesday.
"Of the trades closed out today a fair number were probably spreads put on yesterday between gilts and Bunds and gilts and Matif, but it looks like gilts held up well," said York.
June short sterling held Tuesday's gains and locked in another basis point to settle at 93.42.

"The strip is still looking very optimistic given most people think rates will be higher under the newly independent Bank of England," said a trader at a UK bank. "And June doesn't look like much of a buy since it is only narrowly factoring in another quarter point rate rise."
The Bank will hold its first independent meeting on monetary policy in June. -- Rosemary Bennett +44 171 542 7715
